title: Point-automorphism transport commutes with completed coefficient extension
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite coefficient fields $E\subset L\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $G_F=g^{-1}$ on completed $\mathcal O_F$-module complexes, with the coefficient action through $c_F^{-1}$, and $P_F=Lg_F^*$ for completed derived pullback [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], for $F=E,L$. For $K\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], put $T K=K\widehat\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Write $\sigma^{g,F}$ for the restriction/coprojection maps of [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural].

For a constructible complex $H$ put $C H=H\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$, where $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $\chi_H:C H\to T H$ be the specified completion comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Let $b_K:C G_E K\to G_L C K$ be the canonical inverse-image tensor comparison and let $\beta_K=G_L(\chi_K)b_K\chi_{G_EK}^{-1}:T G_E K\to G_L T K$ be exactly the comparison of [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension]. Let $\varphi_H:\Gamma(s,T H)\to\Gamma(s,H)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ be exactly the sections comparison of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], namely $\varphi_H=(\Gamma(s,\chi_H)\circ\theta_H)^{-1}$, where $\theta_H:\Gamma(s,H)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\to\Gamma(s,CH)$ is the canonical sections-tensor map. All occurrences of $G_EK,P_EK$ here are constructible and derived complete [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Put $\psi_K=\varphi_{G_EK}\Gamma(s,\beta_K)^{-1}$. Then
$$\psi_K\sigma^{g,L}_{TK}=(\sigma^{g,E}_K\otimes1)\varphi_K.$$

Let $\kappa^F_H:G_F H\to P_F H$ be the specified integral comparison [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] and define $t^F_H=\Gamma(s,\kappa^F_H)\sigma^{g,F}_H$. For the canonical $\alpha_K:T(P_EK)\to P_L(TK)$ [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], one has
$$\varphi_{P_EK}\Gamma(s,\alpha_K)^{-1}t^L_{TK}=(t^E_K\otimes1)\varphi_K.$$
After tensoring this equation with $L$, it gives the same compatibility for $t^{E,\mathrm{rat}}_K=t^E_K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ on the raw rationalized categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], under the rational sections and pullback scalar comparisons. These equations are compatible with identity and successive finite coefficient extensions under the canonical associators of the two cited scalar-comparison lemmas. No naturality of $t^F$ in $H$ is asserted here.

proof.text: The hypotheses make $G_EK$ and $P_EK$ bounded constructible and derived complete by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Thus the completion isomorphisms of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] and the natural sections comparisons of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] apply to each of $K,G_EK,P_EK$. Use $\theta_H$ for the ordinary derived sections-tensor map. By [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent], ordinary coefficient extension and sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms, ordinary tensor on representatives computes $C$, and $\theta$ is defined by the termwise sections map even on nonconstructible complexes. In particular no bounded flat representative is needed. Put $\eta_H=\Gamma(s,\chi_H)\theta_H=\varphi_H^{-1}$ for the three complete objects above.

Deligne (1.1.3) and (1.1.7) give the rationalization and transport context, not this completed comparison theorem.

proof.text:
First compare ordinary tensors, before completion. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and do the following termwise calculation on $P$. Put $U=(s,\mathrm{id})$ and $V=(s,g)$. Under the evaluation identification in [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural], $\sigma^g$ is restriction from $U$ to $V$. In each degree test the maps from $\Gamma(s,P)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ on $x\otimes a$. By [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor], $\theta_P$ sends it to the sheafification image of $x\otimes a_s$. The tensor restriction formula in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] sends this to the image of $x|_V\otimes a_s|_V$. The other route first gives $\sigma^{g,E}_P(x)\otimes a$; the local formula for $b$ in [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model] gives precisely the same section under evaluation at $V$. Here the constant coefficient is unchanged: [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] gives $\sigma^g_{R_L}(a_s)=c_L^{-1}(a_s)$, exactly the transported action used by $b$. Pure tensors generate the source module, so the maps agree, degree by degree, and commute with differentials. The tensor-model lemma makes $G_EP$ K-flat and identifies $b_P$ with $b_K$ after localization. Naturality of $\sigma$ for $P\to K$ and the exact descent of [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent] and the representative identification of $b$ in the tensor-model lemma give
$$\Gamma(s,b_K)\theta_{G_EK}(\sigma^{g,E}_K\otimes1)=\sigma^{g,L}_{CK}\theta_K.$$
This uses images of presheaf pure tensors only, and does not assume that arbitrary sheaf tensor sections are sectionwise tensors.

proof.text:
Apply the derived naturality assertion of [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] at coefficient field $L$ to $\chi_K:CK\to TK$. It gives
$$\Gamma(s,G_L\chi_K)\sigma^{g,L}_{CK}=\sigma^{g,L}_{TK}\Gamma(s,\chi_K).$$
Its domain is allowed: that assertion applies to every derived morphism, without constructibility assumptions. By the specified definition of $\beta$ in [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension], Step 2 therefore implies
$$\begin{aligned}
\Gamma(s,\beta_K)\eta_{G_EK}(\sigma^{g,E}_K\otimes1)
&=\Gamma(s,G_L\chi_K)\Gamma(s,b_K)\theta_{G_EK}(\sigma^{g,E}_K\otimes1)\\
&=\sigma^{g,L}_{TK}\Gamma(s,\chi_K)\theta_K
=\sigma^{g,L}_{TK}\eta_K.
\end{aligned}$$
Cancel the invertible maps and use $\eta_H^{-1}=\varphi_H$ from [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. This gives exactly $\varphi_{G_EK}\Gamma(s,\beta_K)^{-1}\sigma^{g,L}_{TK}=(\sigma^{g,E}_K\otimes1)\varphi_K$, the first asserted equation.

proof.text:
The specified-comparison equation of [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension] is $\alpha_K T(\kappa^{E}_K)=\kappa^{L}_{TK}\beta_K$. Since $\alpha_K$ and $\beta_K$ are invertible, applying sections gives
$$\Gamma(s,\alpha_K)^{-1}\Gamma(s,\kappa^{L}_{TK})=\Gamma(s,T(\kappa^{E}_K))\Gamma(s,\beta_K)^{-1}.$$
The map $\kappa^E_K:G_EK\to P_EK$ is the derived morphism specified by [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]; both endpoints satisfy the hypotheses from Step 1. Naturality of $\varphi$ in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], applied to this morphism, now gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\varphi_{P_EK}\Gamma(s,\alpha_K)^{-1}t^L_{TK}
&=(\Gamma(s,\kappa^E_K)\otimes1)\varphi_{G_EK}\Gamma(s,\beta_K)^{-1}\sigma^{g,L}_{TK}\\
&=(\Gamma(s,\kappa^E_K)\otimes1)(\sigma^{g,E}_K\otimes1)\varphi_K
=(t^E_K\otimes1)\varphi_K.
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equality is Step 3. Naturality of $t$ is not used.

proof.text:
For identity and successive extensions, first check the ordinary $b$ maps. Write $C_{L/E}$ for ordinary derived change of coefficients and $a^C$ for its associator. For $E\subset L\subset M$ the local formula of [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model] and the pure-tensor associator of [lem-weil-point-derived-tensor-tower-coherence] give
$$b_{M/E,K}a^C_{G_EK}=G_M(a^C_K)b_{M/L,C_{L/E}K}C_{M/L}(b_{L/E,K}).$$
On a flat-term K-flat model as in Step 2, both routes on the local tensor $((y\otimes a)\otimes b)$ with $y=g^{-1}x$, $a=c_L(g^{-1}a_0)$, $b=c_M(g^{-1}b_0)$, give $g^{-1}(x\otimes a_0b_0)$. Tensor bilinearity and sheafification extend this equality to all sections; the tensor-model lemma identifies these representatives with the derived maps. For $L=E$ the same formula reduces to multiplication, giving the unit equation. There is no completed-tower comparison hidden in this calculation.

proof.text:
Let $A_H:T_{M/L}T_{L/E}H\to T_{M/E}H$ be the integral associator specified in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], namely the ordinary associator conjugated by $\chi$. Substitute $\beta=G(\chi)b\chi_G^{-1}$ from [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension] into Step 5. Naturality and invertibility of $\chi$ from [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] cancel the adjacent $\chi^{-1}\chi$ factors, after moving $C_{M/L}G_L(\chi_{L/E,K})$ past $b_{M/L}$ by the naturality of $b$ in [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model], and give
$$\beta_{M/E,K}A_{G_EK}=G_M(A_K)\beta_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}T_{M/L}(\beta_{L/E,K}).$$
The same cancellation gives the unit equation. Using this equation and the naturality and associator equation for $\varphi$ in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] in the formula $\psi=\varphi_G\Gamma(\beta)^{-1}$ gives
$$\psi_{M/E,K}\Gamma(s,G_M A_K)=a^{\mathrm{mod}}(\psi_{L/E,K}\otimes1)\psi_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}.$$
In this substitution naturality of $\varphi_{M/L}$ is applied to $\beta_{L/E,K}$; thus the middle $T_{M/L}(\beta_{L/E,K})$ cancels as well. This proves the identity and successive-extension compatibility of the first equation. For the second equation, run the same computation with $\alpha$ in place of $\beta$: put $\psi'_K=\varphi_{P_EK}\Gamma(s,\alpha_K)^{-1}$. The composition compatibility of $\alpha$ in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], for the integral associator $A$ above, reads $\alpha_{M/E,K}A_{P_EK}=P_M(A_K)\alpha_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}T_{M/L}(\alpha_{L/E,K})$; with the associator equation of $\varphi$ and naturality of $\varphi_{M/L}$ applied to $\alpha_{L/E,K}$ (Step 1), it gives $\psi'_{M/E,K}\Gamma(s,P_MA_K)=a^{\mathrm{mod}}(\psi'_{L/E,K}\otimes1)\psi'_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}$, and $\psi'=\mathrm{id}$ for $L=E$ by the identity clauses of $\alpha$ and $\varphi$. This is the compatibility of the second equation, whose left side is $\psi'_Kt^L_{TK}$. Module associators: $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto x\otimes ab$.

proof.text: Apply the functor $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}L$ to Step 4. The exactness and derived naturality in [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization] identify each extended source or target by the specified map $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto(n\otimes1)\otimes ab$. Hence the right side becomes $(t^{E,\mathrm{rat}}_K\otimes_E1_L)$ composed with the rational sections comparison of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], and the left side uses the rationalization of the same $\alpha_K$. These are the raw rationalized functors of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], which keep the integral objects and tensor their morphisms with the fraction field. This is the requested rational equation. The unit and mixed integral/field tower equation of the rationalization lemma carry the identity and successive-extension equations of Step 6 to the rational ones, including fractions; no idempotent completion or new choice of comparison is involved.

The generic finite-free completion comparison supplies the specified natural chi isomorphism needed by this coefficient compatibility calculation.
The generic point-sections theorem defines phi and supplies its naturality and coefficient associators; no theorem of the inherited unit supplies this sections comparison.
The generic exact-functor localization theorem permits termwise ordinary tensor and sections computations on arbitrary representatives and their passage to derived categories.
The generic point-sections tensor theorem supplies the balanced pure-tensor formula and the constant-value coefficient sections, not any automorphism compatibility conclusion.
The generic ordinary-tensor associator and its representative formula are used only to check coherence of the specified comparison maps.
The generic operations coefficient-comparison theorem supplies the unit and composition coherence of the specified alpha; this proof does not replace its construction.
The generic module-complex fraction-field tensor comparison supplies exactness and coherence for passing the proved integral equation to raw rationalization.
The general existence theorem supplies a flat-term K-flat resolution for the ordinary tensor calculation; it is used solely as a resolution tool, not as a replacement proof route.
